name: Game Manager

attribute.tooltip: Seconds between the killing blow and the YOU DIED banner.
Seconds between the killing blow and the respawn at the bonfire.
Template instantiated where the player died, carrying their souls.
Off, no blood at all: no spray and no decals.

The blood thrown off a wound, spawned where the hit struck and scaled with it (particles in the kit; the Valley's is a lit flipbook of an FX Creator liquid simulation). Empty: no spray, the decal alone.
The spatter decal thrown along the blow.
Metres along the blow from the target to the spatter decal's centre (at a full-size hit).
Blood decals alive at once. The oldest goes first, so a long fight cannot pile up draws.
Damage that leaves a full-size splat; less shrinks it, more grows it (0.6x to 1.6x).
Name of the reward pickup revealed once the boss falls.
Name of the lore message revealed once the boss falls.
Off, every blow plays at full speed.
Game speed during a hit-stop: 0.2 is 80% slower.
Real seconds a killing blow holds the hit-stop, at least.
Log a one-off warning when the project's input map lacks the souls actions.

name: Player

attribute.tooltip: Fraction of incoming damage ignored, 0..0.9.
The weapons the player starts with, by template. F swaps between them.
Socket on this character's skeleton the weapons attach to.
Child group the weapons are spawned under (this node itself when there is none).
The held weapon's display name, for the HUD.
Let go of the held weapon on death, as a physics body (see dropWeapon).
The dropped weapon's mass, kg.
The steepest ground, in degrees, this character can walk UP. On anything steeper it can still move across the slope or down it, but not climb (see limitClimb). The engine's own limit is 60°.

Attacks, rolls and reactions are played by TRIGGER, by name (`_playTrigger`): the animator has a state each one enters, which leaves on its own at the clip's end. The graph owns every clip, its speed and its blends; the script owns the gameplay, and asks the animator how long what a trigger plays lasts (`Animator.triggerInfo`) and whether it still plays (`Animator.activeTrigger`). These two take the one-shot's layer back to rest from anything: with its blend-out, and at once.
Estus Shards raise it for good.
HP restored per flask, spread over `estusHealSeconds`.
HP at Vigor 10. Each point to 30 adds `hpPerVigor`, then the curve flattens.
Stamina at Endurance 10, plus `staminaPerEndurance` per point to 40.

variables.name: waterNotice
variables.default: Can't roll or sprint in water

attribute.tooltip: Shown once on wading in: water slows you and stops rolls and sprints.
Throttle while locked on: strafing is slower than running.
Ramp while freely moving. Actions snap (0) so a roll starts at full speed.
Degrees per second the body turns toward a locked target while standing.
After sprinting to empty, sprint stays locked until stamina recovers to this.

Move by the roll's OWN travel (the Roll state extracts its clip's root travel) instead of the rollSpeed curve above: the body covers exactly the ground the dive does, through its own collision, for as long as the state lasts. The roll always faces the way it goes -- there is only a forward roll.
Reversing at a run plays a planted 180° turn instead of spinning on the spot. Off: the plain turn.
Degrees between where the player is running and where the stick now points that count as reversing.
Running at least this fast (m/s); a walker just turns.
Share of the turn spent braking to a stop before pushing off the other way.
The animator parameters the turn holds on a straight-ahead run underneath its clip (see _pinRunPose): the character's measured speed and direction, which would otherwise drop to Idle at the plant.
After the turn, the longest the speed parameter keeps following the body while the measured speed catches up.
Hold Roll longer than this while moving and it becomes a sprint instead of a roll.
A hit at or above this much damage is a heavy stagger with knockback; below, a flinch.
Real seconds of hit-stop when a hit lands on the player (the GameManager's), light and heavy.
A swing that meets a wall (a `blocksSwings` body) before any enemy bounces off it for this long.
Falling below this height is death.
The running 180° turn, turning right and turning left (Left falls back to Right when it is missing).
Fallback seconds into the drink clip at which the heal starts when it has no `drink` event.
Played when a swing bounces off a wall.
A weapon swap: the layer sheathes the one in hand, then draws the next. The weapon changes on the sheathe clip's `swap` event (or as the draw begins, when the clip has none).
Sitting at a bonfire: a looping state, left on SoulsCharacter's `stopTrigger`.

Seconds the combat stance holds after the last blow given or taken (once no enemy is engaged and nothing is locked). While `inCombat`, the animator's `InCombat` swaps the idle for the Longsword's guard and keeps both hands on the hilt while moving.
How often the engaged enemies are looked for, seconds.

name: Lock-On Camera

attribute.tooltip: Seconds the target may stay hidden behind geometry before the lock lets go.
Seconds between two target switches, so one flick switches once.
Right-stick deflection (scaled ×4 in the map) that counts as a flick.
Mouse speed, in pixels per SECOND, that counts as a flick. A per-frame pixel threshold made switching targets harder the higher the frame rate, since the same flick is spread over more frames.
Pitch limits while locked (positive looks down). Keeps a tall boss from flipping the camera.
When the target dies, the lock jumps to another enemy only if one is this close.
Boom length while locked: closer than the free camera, for a tighter view of the fight.
Pivot offset while locked (rig space: +X is the rig's LEFT, +Y up) — negative X, so the camera sits over the RIGHT shoulder and the target is framed past it.
Seconds the camera takes to move in on a lock, and back out on release.
